summary: Steam is a leaner, friendlier reworking of Age of Steam: you bid for turn order, build track networks, and deliver goods cubes for points or income, but the harsh forced-income-reduction of the original is replaced by an optional loan mechanism. It plays as a tight, cutthroat economic puzzle where efficient route-building and timing your deliveries matter more than raw luck.
praised: More forgiving and accessible than Age of Steam while keeping the same core tension
Double-sided board and modular map system give strong replayability
Tight, efficient rules with meaningful decisions every turn
Satisfying network-building and delivery optimization puzzle
criticised: Still very cutthroat and can be brutal for new players who fall behind economically
Auction/bidding start can feel swingy or unintuitive to newcomers
High player interaction on the shared map leads to analysis paralysis in some groups
Some feel it lost a bit of the original Age of Steam's harsher, more strategic bite

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial over track and delivery routes

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Victory points come almost entirely from successful goods deliveries, with efficient track building and income management as the main lever to maximize them
